missionPremise: OPS-24 Ruling 14 (_decisions/2026-09-18_phase0_closeout_rulings.md): the source with the most recent effective date supplies a setback value, tier breaks ties only on equal or unreadable dates, dates are read at source and never assumed from source kind, and an unreadable date produces a conflict row carrying both values rather than a silent pick. The mechanism is the standing decision _decisions/2026-09-13_share_the_most_current_setback_resolver.md: ONE resolver in ONE package, @empressaio/setback-corpus/resolve. The probe measured what its absence cost: PANEL-DRAW-TABLE-DISAGREE on 7 parcels with no exemptions.
completionPredicate: For each of the 7 measured parcels the card and the drawing route pick among the same candidates by the same rule through the shared resolver, serve the same 4-tuple, and declare the R-1 conflict row wherever the winning date is unreadable; the card has exactly one table home with the vendored copy retired behind a guard; a divergence test pins the 7 tuples in both repos and fails when either side changes alone; and surface-probe.mjs --rows P-254 reads zero for the class after deploy.
scopeBasis: Only the two setback-resolution paths for these 7 parcels and the table home beneath them -- the card's facet bake in hauska-map apps/property-explorer/api/_lib and the route's buildable-envelope path in legacy-design-tools artifacts/api-server/src/lib/buildableEnvelope plus its adapter district mapping. The card's resolution had to land on option (b) of the P-339/P-341 handover (resolve through the shared resolver) rather than (a) (echo the route), because the standing decision names one resolver for every producer and because the register records the draw route answering 504 under load. Nothing else is touched: no factory file, no MCP file, no deployed surface, no store row, and no bake.
theSourceTable: See CP1 (_inbox/2026-09-19_p340-card-route-table_cp1.json) for the full per-subject table required by build item 1 -- each side's source, table, row and date for all 7 -- measured from live endpoints before any code. Its shape in one line: 5 subjects were a MISSING/DIFFERING CORNER AXIS and 2 were a WHOLLY DIFFERENT TABLE, matching the dispatch's own split; no date exists on any candidate on either side (no table carries an effectiveDate, every atom carries vintage=null), which is why the unreadable-date branch is the live one for this class and why the settlement is by TIER with a conflict row rather than by date.
theRetirementDecision: codified-setback-from-zoning.ts and api/_lib/setback-tables/*.json (4 jurisdiction files: austin-tx 9 rows, elgin-development-code, pflugerville-tx, san-antonio-tx) are RETIRED BY DECLINE and deleted -- the dispatch's first branch, not the 'kept for a named reason' one, because a second home for setback law beside the shared corpus is the defect class this row exists to close and the Austin copy had already drifted from the corpus's own note (its MF-2/MF-3 front yard is the pre-correction 15 ft; the corpus's note records the current Municode table states 25 ft as a KNOWN CONFLICT NOT TOUCHED). The guard is setback-corpus-retirement.test.ts, which walks the app's whole source tree and fails if the module is imported again, if api/_lib/setback-tables/ exists, or if any file other than setback-corpus-table.ts reads the bare corpus root.

fleetMemory.LESSON: A surface disagreement can be a MISSING TABLE, not a wrong number: on 5 of these 7 subjects the card had no table for that city at all and served the bake snapshot while the route read a codified row. Compare the two SOURCE KINDS and the jurisdiction coverage before comparing values -- two tables can never disagree on a row one of them does not have.

The corner axis is the axis most easily lost: an adapter that emits side_corner_ft only when it differs from the side yard drops a real standard whenever the two are equal, and the served '-' reads like an honest absence. All 5 of this lane's axis defects had corner == side in the atom.

P-331's cross-repo drift checker reads the sibling's WORKING TREE before its HEAD, so a stale sibling checkout yields DRIFT_MARKER_MISSING (exit 2) that looks like drift. Reproduce CI with a scratch worktree at origin/main, not with whatever checkout happens to be on disk.
